page.layout: One printed page (left-hand, p. 274). Running head at the top, then one text column with marginal notes in the left margin, beside the lines at the top of the column. No text below the column.

main_text.p: ctor pag.97. negat hinc sequi, Onesimum quendam Gaij successorem Epheso minimè praefuisse, cùm Ignatius ad martyrium tractus est: Nempe fieri posse putat Vir doctus duos fuisse Onesimos, quorum alter sub Domitiano Martyr obierit, alter verò Gaio Episcopo Ephesino successerit, eíque Ecclesiae praefuerit, dum Ignatius vinctus Romam ducebatur ; Vsser. Not. in Epist. Ignat. ad Ephes. Not. 9. pag. 5.Reverendissimus Vsserius hunc nodum paulò aliter solvit , suspicatur videlicet duos fuisse Onesimos, utrúmque Ephesi Episcopum, unum Seniorem, Pauli discipulum, sub Domitiano passum: alterum Gaij successorem, Ignatio superstitem. Dallæus huic distinctioni sic occurrit pag. 316. Sed hæc ne admittantur, prohibet primò Bedæ, Adonis, Notkeri, & aliorum fides, qui istum ab Ignatio Epistolico memoratum Onesimum magno omnes consensu Pauli discipulum fuisse affirmant. Pearsonius ait se talem consensum non reperire; quia solus Ado de Ignatij Onesimo mentionem facit in libello de festivitatibus Apostolorum ad XIIII. Kalend. Mart. Reliqui eundem Onesimum Philemonis servum à B. Paulo Ephesinae Ecclesiae post Timotheum constitutum fuisse Episcopum tradunt, nullâ Ignatij mentione factâ; observat praeterea idem Pearsonius Adonem qui Onesimum S.

page.notes: Printed text ends mid-sentence at "S." and the running text continues on the next page. The long s is printed like f in the scan and is transcribed as s. The word "Epheso" is printed with a letter o whose form is slightly doubtful; it is transcribed as Latin o. Only the marginal note block at the left was treated as a single note, since its lines run together without separation.
